sector: Consumer Discretionary / Restaurants (Quick Service / Fast Casual)
data_availability_note: Analysis is grounded in the company's own NZX filings held locally in research/BFG.NZ/Extracted/ (FY2018-FY2026 annual/preliminary results and H1-2018 through H1-2025 half-year reports), supplemented by web search for post-balance-date developments. Key figures verified directly against the FY2026 preliminary result (year ended 31 March 2026): operating revenue NZ$24.845m, NPAT NZ$1,968,937 (+91.8%), total system sales NZ$111.4m (+2.93%), 62 NZ BurgerFuel restaurants, 3 Shake Out stores plus 29 virtual kitchens, 1 Winner Winner store, Middle East system sales -26% with the Jubail (Saudi) closure announced 16 May 2026. An earlier internal note claiming BFG delisted from the NZX in 2021 is incorrect: the stock trades on the NZSE at ~NZ$0.32 as at 8 August 2026.
overview: Burger Fuel Group Limited is a New Zealand-based franchisor and, to a diminishing extent, operator of gourmet burger and fast-casual restaurants, trading on the NZX under BFG. The group owns three brands - BurgerFuel (the core, ~90%+ of system sales), and two smaller New Zealand concepts, Shake Out (a capital-light virtual-kitchen milkshake/dessert brand) and Winner Winner (a fried chicken concept) - alongside a legacy, now largely reduced, Middle East master-franchise footprint in the UAE and Saudi Arabia. It is an extreme micro-cap (~NZ$11-12M market capitalisation, share price ~NZ$0.30-0.34 in mid-2026) with a highly concentrated shareholder register.

business_model.summary: BFG earns franchise/royalty income and other fees (marketing levies, initial franchise fees, supply-chain margin) from a network of predominantly franchisee-owned BurgerFuel restaurants in New Zealand, supplemented by a small number of company-owned/operated stores and virtual kitchens, plus a shrinking Middle East master-franchise royalty stream. Total System Sales (sales generated across the whole network, franchised and owned) is the headline KPI management reports ($111.4M in FY2026); Group reported revenue ($25.6M in FY2026, of which $24.845M was operating revenue) captures only BFG's own royalties, company-store sales and fees - not full franchisee turnover. The FY2026 sale of the company-owned BurgerFuel Ponsonby store into franchising (generating a $288K one-off gain) is consistent with a continued shift toward an asset-light franchisor model. Shake Out is deliberately kept capital-light via 'virtual kitchens' operated out of existing BurgerFuel sites (29 virtual kitchens vs only 3 standalone Shake Out stores at FY2026), generating incremental sales with minimal incremental labour or capex. The company is also investing in proprietary online ordering/IT platforms (BurgerFuel ordering platform v2 launched January 2026; a 'White Label' platform in pilot to license the technology for external revenue).

revenue_streams.name: BurgerFuel New Zealand (franchise royalties, fees, remaining company stores)
revenue_streams.note: 62 NZ BurgerFuel restaurants at FY2026 year end; NZ system sales $108M, +4.12% YoY; core driver of Group revenue and profit

revenue_streams.name: Middle East (UAE/Saudi Arabia master franchise royalties)
revenue_streams.note: System sales ~$3.28M in FY2026 (down 26% YoY), ~2.95% of Group system sales; 3 stores in UAE (1 BurgerFuel WTC + 1 food truck + 1 Shake Out) and 1 in Saudi Arabia (Amwaj) after the Jubail store closed May 2026

revenue_streams.name: Shake Out (virtual kitchens + standalone stores)
revenue_streams.note: Sales +20% in FY2026; 3 standalone stores plus 29 virtual kitchens operated inside existing BurgerFuel locations - capital-light incremental revenue

revenue_streams.name: Winner Winner (fried chicken)
revenue_streams.note: Only 1 restaurant operating at FY2026 year end; management commentary indicates the Group is reducing exposure to this underperforming brand

business_model.customer_type: B2B (franchisees paying royalties/fees) plus B2C end-consumers at company-owned stores and virtual kitchens
business_model.geographic_mix: New Zealand ~97% of system sales (66 restaurants across 3 brands); Middle East (UAE + Saudi Arabia) ~3% and shrinking

main_competitors: Restaurant Brands NZ (KFC, Pizza Hut, Carl's Jr, Taco Bell NZ franchisee)
Domestic fried-chicken and QSR chains (for Winner Winner)
competitive_position.market_position: Small, domestically focused niche player in New Zealand's gourmet/premium burger segment; far smaller in scale than the major multinational-backed QSR chains (Restaurant Brands, McDonald's) that dominate NZ fast food by store count and marketing budget

moat_factors.description: BurgerFuel has an established premium, 'gourmet'/better-burger positioning in NZ built since 1995, distinct from the mainstream multinational chains
Asset-light royalty model (reinforced by the Ponsonby store sale) generates relatively stable fee income with lower capital intensity than company-operated restaurants
66 restaurants across three brands is small versus multinational-backed competitors; limited purchasing power and marketing scale
Franchise agreements create some lock-in, but the brand's small scale and thin economics leave franchisees more exposed to input cost inflation than larger-network peers

weaknesses: Very small scale relative to multinational-backed NZ QSR competitors limits negotiating power on beef, ingredients and fit-out costs
Heavy reliance on a single small, mature domestic market (New Zealand) for the vast majority of system sales
Winner Winner brand has failed to gain traction (down to a single restaurant) and Middle East operations are in structural decline
Two consecutive years (FY2024, FY2025) of earnings were materially depressed by internal shareholder litigation costs, reflecting governance/register risk rather than trading weakness

growth_drivers: Expansion of the capital-light Shake Out virtual-kitchen model inside existing BurgerFuel stores (sales +20% in FY2026, 29 virtual kitchens)
New BurgerFuel store openings planned for FY2027 (Huapai, September 2026; Richmond Nelson, November 2026) in what management describes as high-potential locations
Continued shift toward an asset-light franchisor model (sale of the company-owned Ponsonby store into franchising, Dec 2025) freeing capital and reducing direct operating risk

Investment in proprietary IT/online ordering platforms (BurgerFuel ordering platform v2, launched January 2026) and a 'White Label' platform being piloted to license the technology to third parties for incremental, higher-margin revenue
Exploration of vertical integration into ingredient production/supply chain to offset input-cost inflation and protect margins
Resolution (for now) of the multi-year shareholder litigation removes a recurring drag on reported profit, unlocking a cleaner earnings base going into FY2027

business.description: Market capitalisation of roughly NZ$11-12M and a free float reduced further by ~66% controlling ownership (Mason Roberts Holdings/Josef Roberts) makes the stock thinly traded, with wide bid/ask spreads and high price volatility on small volumes

~97% of system sales come from New Zealand; the business has essentially no material diversification benefit from its residual Middle East operations, leaving it fully exposed to NZ consumer and hospitality-sector conditions

As a franchisor, BFG's royalty income depends on the financial health of its NZ franchisees, who face the same cost inflation (beef, fuel, labour) and soft discretionary spending pressures management flags for FY2027

business.risk: Winner Winner brand failure / Middle East runoff
business.description: Winner Winner has shrunk to a single restaurant and the Middle East network (down to 3-4 stores, sales -26% in FY2026, ~3% of system sales) continues to contract; further write-downs or exit costs are possible

The FY2024/FY2025 scheme-of-arrangement dispute (see below) demonstrates the concentrated-ownership register can generate large, recurring legal costs that materially swing reported profit; renewed disputes with minority or founder-aligned shareholders cannot be ruled out

financial.description: Group operating revenue of ~$24.8M and net profit of ~$2.0M in FY2026 (BFG's best year to date) leaves little buffer to absorb cost shocks or a sales downturn

The FY2026 91.8% profit increase was aided by a $288K one-off gain on the Ponsonby store sale and by the year-on-year drop-off in legal costs versus FY2024/FY2025 - both are non-repeating items that inflate the growth rate versus underlying trading
BFG has no record of paying dividends, so investor returns depend entirely on capital appreciation in an illiquid, thinly covered stock

regulatory.risk: Companies Act / Takeovers Panel scrutiny of controlling shareholder actions
regulatory.description: The 2023-2024 capital-return scheme of arrangement drew a High Court challenge and NZ Shareholders' Association scrutiny over disclosure adequacy and treatment of the controlling shareholder (Mason Roberts Holdings/Josef Roberts, ~66%) versus minorities; the Court found 'process failures' even while approving the scheme, signalling ongoing governance/disclosure risk for future related-party or capital-structure transactions
Management explicitly flagged FY2026/27 disruption from regional instability (including the Iran conflict) affecting the UAE/Saudi Arabia master-franchise business

macro.description: Management explicitly cites 'ongoing hurdles within the broader economic environment and particularly the hospitality sector' and guided FY2027 system sales to be roughly flat; discretionary QSR spending is highly sensitive to a soft NZ economy
Management flagged rising beef prices (driven by strong US demand), fuel and ingredient inflation as a key FY2027 margin risk for both company operations and franchisees
As a discretionary, mid-price dining category, BurgerFuel/Shake Out/Winner Winner sales are sensitive to NZ household disposable income, mortgage rates and consumer confidence

macro.risk: Extended equipment lead times / supply chain
macro.description: Management noted extended global lead times for store equipment as a constraint on new-store rollout timing

macro_factors.industry_outlook: New Zealand QSR/fast-casual dining is a mature, low-growth, highly competitive market dominated by larger multinational-backed operators (Restaurant Brands, McDonald's, Burger King). Management's own FY2027 guidance is for system sales to be 'roughly flat' given the challenging economic and hospitality-sector backdrop, alongside emerging cost inflation.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - discretionary dining spend, though the franchise-royalty revenue stream is somewhat more stable/recurring than company-owned-store economics
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity via NZ consumer discretionary spending and franchisee financing costs for new store fit-outs
key_input_costs: Beef (flagged as rising due to strong US demand)

recent_developments.event: Sale of the company-owned BurgerFuel Ponsonby store into franchising, generating a one-off $288K gain ($140K asset gain plus $148K lease wind-down benefit) - consistent with continued shift to an asset-light franchisor model
Launch of upgraded BurgerFuel proprietary online ordering platform (v2); a 'White Label' version of the platform is in pilot to potentially license to third parties for additional revenue
Saudi Arabia's Jubail BurgerFuel store closed, leaving only the Amwaj store in Saudi Arabia alongside 3 UAE locations - continued contraction of the Middle East master-franchise footprint

FY2026 (year ended 31 March 2026) preliminary results released: net profit after tax $1,968,937 (+91.8% YoY), described by management as the Group's best result to date; Total System Sales $111.4M (+2.93%); Group revenue $25.6M (+2.63%); NZ system sales +4.12% to $108M while Middle East system sales fell 26% to $3.28M (~3% of total)

Management issued cautious FY2027 guidance: system sales expected to be roughly flat given a 'far more challenging operating environment,' rising beef/fuel/ingredient costs, and continued Middle East instability (including fallout from the Iran conflict) with 'no material revenue' being relied upon from that region
New store openings confirmed for FY2027: BurgerFuel Huapai (September 2026) and BurgerFuel Richmond, Nelson (November 2026)

Implementation of the Court-approved capital return: NZ$0.27 paid per share for 30% of each shareholder's shares cancelled (~$4.077M total), following High Court approval on 8 May 2024 despite a shareholder (Mason Trustee Ltd, associated with founder Chris Mason) opposition; the Court found 'process failures' in disclosure even while approving the scheme and ordered BFG to pay Mason Trustee Ltd's costs

guidance.management_commentary: Management characterised FY2026 as the Group's 'best result to date' notwithstanding 'ongoing hurdles within the broader economic environment and particularly the hospitality sector,' but was explicitly cautious on FY2027, warning of a 'far more challenging operating environment,' flat system sales, rising input costs, and high, unpredictable Middle East geopolitical risk. Strategic priorities highlighted were continued IT platform investment (including a 'White Label' licensing opportunity), capital-light expansion of Shake Out virtual kitchens, selective new BurgerFuel store openings, and exploring vertical integration into ingredient supply to protect margins.

bull_case: FY2026 delivered the company's best-ever net profit ($1.97M, +91.8%) with the two-year drag of shareholder litigation costs now largely behind it, potentially unlocking a cleaner, higher earnings base

Continued shift to an asset-light franchisor model (Ponsonby store sale) and capital-light Shake Out virtual-kitchen expansion (+20% sales, 29 virtual kitchens) offer margin-accretive growth without heavy new capex
New IT ordering platform (v2) and a 'White Label' licensing pilot could open an incremental, higher-margin revenue stream if commercialised
New store pipeline (Huapai, Richmond Nelson) shows the core NZ BurgerFuel brand still has organic expansion runway despite the tough macro backdrop
Company holds a debt-light balance sheet with 'strong' cash, providing flexibility for further acquisitions, joint ventures or opportunistic buybacks
bear_case: Extreme micro-cap illiquidity and a ~66% controlling shareholder (Mason Roberts Holdings/Josef Roberts) leave minority holders with limited influence, thin trading volumes, and demonstrated governance/disclosure risk (the 2023-24 scheme-of-arrangement dispute, which the High Court found involved 'process failures')

Management's own FY2027 guidance calls for roughly flat system sales and a 'far more challenging operating environment,' with rising beef, fuel and ingredient costs pressuring margins just as the FY2026 profit tailwinds (lower legal costs, one-off Ponsonby gain) will not repeat

Near-total dependence (~97% of system sales) on the small, mature New Zealand market with no meaningful geographic diversification; the Middle East business continues to shrink (-26% in FY2026) amid regional instability
Winner Winner brand has effectively failed (down to one restaurant) and the company pays no dividend, meaning returns rely solely on capital appreciation in a stock with little analyst coverage

Underlying FY2026 profit growth is flattered by non-recurring items (the $288K Ponsonby gain and the year-on-year fall in legal costs versus FY2024/25), making the reported 91.8% profit growth rate a poor guide to sustainable earnings power
